newsitem.title: GERMANY: Compaq says saw Q2 surge in European sales.
newsitem.headline: Compaq says saw Q2 surge in European sales.

text.p: Compaq Computer Corp said on Thursday European sales in the second quarter rose 41 percent in unit terms, and 21 percent in dollar values.
"It was a very good quarter," Compaq European chief Andreas Barth told Reuters in an interview. "We had phenomenal unit growth."
In local currencies, European sales rose 32 percent. "We lost some value because the dollar was so strong," Barth said.
Growth was especially strong across northern Europe, as unit sales rose 41 percent in Germany, 36 percent in France and 38 percent in Britain.
Barth also said he was "confident" about the second half outlook for the region.
"We have 130 new products coming out in the second half," he said. "We are trying to drive our (market) share. We want to really maximise our revenue."

He said profitability in Europe was in line with Compaq's corporate results, and would be helped by a shift to a build-to-order manufacturing process. Compaq would use that cost-reducing process to produce new home PCs due this summer, and new corporate PCs due in the fall.

Earlier today, the Houston, Texas, company reported second quarter earnings of $1.48 per share, excluding a $0.73 per-share charge related to an acquisition. Sales in the quarter rose 25 percent to $5.01 billion.
